scope: Proposition 11.30 (Acyclic components admit cheap circuits) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 155. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the simultaneous all-seed construction of Lemma 11.6, the address-occupation estimate, Corollary 10.20, and Remark 10.21. Also use Propositions 7.16 and 7.18, the bilateral interior crossing comparison of Corollary 9.13, and Proposition 6.9. Fix 1 < a0 < a < b and 0 < s′ < s. For a uniform view level in [aNj, bNj], the probability that a base belongs to an acyclic combined center component but has no genuine surrounding circuit with the cost and time bounds of Proposition 11.28 tends to zero. The circuit may be confined to any base spatial neighborhood on which the finite-chain typicality cutoff holds.
